patch.value: Destination census rows cite terminal consolidation owners for five live commands, so the grammar gate certifies consolidations no open item will deliver

## Observed
PM_COMMAND_DESTINATION_CONTRACTS in src/sdk/cli-contracts/grammar-contracts.ts carries consolidation rows whose named owner is a terminal item: assurance, config, profile and schema name pm-6apl (closed; it delivered the ops namespace and never touched these four), and history-author-acknowledge names pm-tqel (closed; it consolidated the history-* spellings and left this one at the root). init names the epic pm-n7rr rather than pm-npr3, the open item whose acceptance criteria decide the customization family. verifyPmCliGrammar and the command-grammar gate check that every live command has a destination row and that stale rows are removed; neither reads the owner's status, so a consolidation whose owner closed without delivering it is certified indefinitely.

## Why it matters
ADR pm-pbyu rule 8 allows a live command to remain only under a target noun, a tracked consolidation owner, a package owner, or a reasoned keep-as-is exception. A closed owner is none of those. The census is the artifact agents and the surface ceiling rely on to know what still moves; five commands currently read as in-flight consolidations that no open item will deliver.

## Non-goals
Deciding where assurance and history-author-acknowledge land is the delivery task filed beside this issue; deciding init/config/schema/profile stays pm-npr3.

verifyPmCliGrammar or the command-grammar gate reports a terminal_consolidation_owner finding when a consolidation row's owner is closed, canceled or missing and the command is not carried by the alias relocation table, with a negative-control fixture; config, profile, schema and init rows name pm-npr3; assurance and history-author-acknowledge rows name the open delivery task filed beside this issue; the contracts fixture is regenerated; The gate's negative control proves a stale-owner row fails upward in CI
Every consolidation row names an open owner or is reclassified; the grammar verification reports a finding when a consolidation owner is terminal or unknown.
